newsitem.title: USA: Florida appeal court rules against tobacco firms.
newsitem.headline: Florida appeal court rules against tobacco firms.

text.p: A Florida court Wednesday upheld a ruling allowing the state to use documents obtained from Brooke Group Ltd.'s Liggett Group in its lawsuit against the tobacco industry.

The ruling was a defeat for the tobacco companies, which had claimed the documents were protected by attorney-client privilege. Attorneys for the state successfully argued that the documents were exempt from that privilege because they involved alleged plans to commit a crime or fraud.

The ruling involves 13 Liggett documents dating from 1963 to 1988. They include memos on trial strategy, a 1964 consumer survey, a 1966 letter on the status of special company projects and a 1978 letter about carbon monoxide analysis.
The ruling was issued by Florida's 4th District Court of Appeals.

A special master advised after a two-day hearing in April that some of the documents should be admitted as evidence. Circuit Judge Harold Cohen, who will preside over the trial in Florida's lawsuit to recoup the public cost of treating smoking-related illnesses, subsequently allowed all 13 to be admitted.

The tobacco companies appealed, arguing that Cohen had applied overly broad standards. But the appeals court said "The special master found that there was evidence that the defendants hid from and misrepresented to the public the health risks of smoking and that their conduct constituted a fraud on the public."
The appeals court ruling also said there was evidence that the tobacco companies "utilized their attorneys in carrying out their misrepresentations."
